Fuels, regions and months

Source: vignettes/articles/across-dimensions.Rmd
across-dimensions.Rmd

This article needs geoscales and timescales 0.7 or later, energypal and ggplot2 installed; its outputs appear on the package site once they are available.

Three scales, one vocabulary

A fuel-use table has three dimensions a model cares about: which fuel, where, when. Each is a nested scale – the fuel taxonomy the core ships, and the classes of two sibling packages built on the same core – and each attaches to a table under its own name:

es  <- read_scale("carriers")          # fuels:   group > carrier > fuel
gs  <- geoscale_example()              # regions: country > state > zone > atom
cal <- calendar("m12")                 # time:    MONTH

scale_units(es, "carrier")
geoscale_regions(gs, "country")
calendar_timeslices(cal)

A fuel-use table

Twelve months of fuel use in six regions for five fuels, in kilotonnes. The numbers are made up but shaped: coal and gas follow a heating season, the size of each region scales its use.

use <- expand.grid(
  atom = geoscale_regions(gs)[geoscale_regions(gs) != "ROW"],
  timeslice = calendar_timeslices(cal),
  fuel = c("Anthracite", "Lignite", "DistillateFuelOil", "NaturalGas",
           "Biodiesel"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
base <- c(Anthracite = 2, Lignite = 6, DistillateFuelOil = 1.5,
          NaturalGas = 4, Biodiesel = 0.3)
seasonal <- c(Anthracite = 0.6, Lignite = 0.6, DistillateFuelOil = 0.1,
              NaturalGas = 0.8, Biodiesel = 0)
size <- geoscale_leaftable(gs) |>
  transmute(atom, size = km2 / mean(km2))
use <- use |>
  left_join(size, by = "atom") |>
  mutate(
    month = match(timeslice, calendar_timeslices(cal)),
    kt = base[fuel] * size *
      (1 + seasonal[fuel] * cos(2 * pi * (month - 1) / 12))
  ) |>
  select(atom, timeslice, fuel, kt)
head(use)

Attach all three

Each join adds columns prefixed by the scale’s name, so the three never collide and a reader can see which scale a column came from:

labelled <- use |>
  join_scale(es, frame = "fuel", attach = TRUE) |>
  join_geoscale(gs = gs, geoframe = "atom", geoframes = TRUE) |>
  join_calendar(calendar = cal, meta = TRUE)
names(labelled)
head(labelled, 3)

carriers.carrier and carriers.group come from the fuel scale, example.country and friends from the GeoScale, m12.share and m12.weight (hours) from the Calendar.

Mass to energy to CO2

The fuel scale carries the IPCC 2006 net calorific value (GJ/t) and CO2 factor (kg/TJ) for these five fuels. Each conversion is one call, keyed by fuel, and the factor applied is reported alongside the result:

energy <- use |>
  mutate(t = kt * 1e3) |>
  select(atom, timeslice, fuel, t) |>
  convert_scale(es, "lhv", from_unit = "t", to_unit = "GJ") |>
  transmute(atom, timeslice, fuel, tj = t / 1e3)

co2 <- energy |>
  convert_scale(es, "ef_co2", from_unit = "TJ", to_unit = "kg") |>
  rename(kg_co2 = tj) |>                 # the converted column: kg CO2
  transmute(atom, timeslice, fuel, tj = energy$tj, kt_co2 = kg_co2 / 1e6)
head(co2, 3)

Aggregate along any dimension

Every scale aggregates with the same verb and the same rules. Columns the scale does not know (the other dimensions’ keys) are carried through as identifiers. One registration covers all three dimensions:

register_scale_rule("tj", "sum")
register_scale_rule("kt_co2", "sum")

By carrier and month – the fuel dimension collapses, region and month stay:

by_carrier <- co2 |>
  recast_scale(es, source = "fuel", target = "carrier",
               missing_sources = "ignore") |>
  filter(!is.na(tj))
head(by_carrier, 3)
sum(by_carrier$tj) - sum(co2$tj)

The table reports five of the 71 fuels. With missing_sources = "ignore" the others count as unused rather than unknown, and the total is conserved – the difference above is zero.

By country – the pipeline verb recast() dispatches on whichever scale it is handed, so the two aggregations chain:

by_country <- co2 |>
  recast(es, target = "carrier", missing_sources = "ignore") |>
  filter(!is.na(tj)) |>
  recast(gs, target = "country")
by_country |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(tj = sum(tj), kt_co2 = sum(kt_co2))

By quarter – a calendar recast needs the year, to place the months on real dates:

by_quarter <- by_carrier |>
  select(carrier, atom, timeslice, tj, kt_co2) |>
  recast_calendar(source = cal, target = calendar("q4"), year = 2024)
head(by_quarter, 4)
sum(by_quarter$tj) - sum(by_carrier$tj)

Draw it with energypal’s colours

energypal’s carriers palette is the same taxonomy, so the carrier ids map straight onto its colours with no relabelling:

by_carrier |>
  group_by(timeslice, carrier) |>
  summarise(tj = sum(tj), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = timeslice, y = tj, fill = carrier)) +
  geom_col() +
  energypal::scale_fill_energy(palette = "carriers",
                               label_style = "short") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "TJ", fill = NULL,
       title = "Energy use by month and carrier") +
  theme_minimal()
by_country |>
  group_by(country, carrier) |>
  summarise(kt_co2 = sum(kt_co2), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = country, y = kt_co2, fill = carrier)) +
  geom_col() +
  energypal::scale_fill_energy(palette = "carriers",
                               label_style = "short") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "kt CO2", fill = NULL,
       title = "CO2 by country and carrier") +
  theme_minimal()

The GeoScale draws its own hierarchy with data attached – CO2 summed to every geoframe at once:

co2_by_atom <- co2 |>
  group_by(atom) |>
  summarise(kt_co2 = sum(kt_co2), .groups = "drop")
geoscale_autoplot(gs, data = co2_by_atom, z = "kt_co2", rule = "sum")

Matching labels from a statistical source

Real sources spell carriers their own way. energypal ships a slice of Our World in Data’s electricity mix; its source labels resolve against the fuel scale’s names and aliases exactly, with frame = "carrier" settling the names that exist at two frames (Nuclear, Other):

mix <- energypal::owid_energy_mix
matched <- scale_match(es, unique(mix$source), frame = "carrier")
matched

Join the resolved id on and the palette applies:

mix |>
  filter(year == 2024) |>
  left_join(matched |> select(source = label, carrier = unit),
            by = "source") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = country, y = generation_twh, fill = carrier)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  energypal::scale_fill_energy(palette = "carriers",
                               label_style = "short") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "share of generation", fill = NULL,
       title = "Electricity generation mix, 2024 (OWID)") +
  theme_minimal()

What each package did

package contributed
fuels nestedscales (carriers) the taxonomy, calorific values, CO2 factors, label matching
regions geoscales the region hierarchy, aggregation to countries, the icicle
time timescales month shares and hours, aggregation to quarters
colours energypal one palette for every figure, by carrier id

The core is what lets one table carry all three and lets recast() chain across them.
